blogs.title: The Wall of Expert Testimony: Why Finesse v. AT&T Shows the Risk of Ambiguous Mapping
blogs.description: This post dissects the Federal Circuit's reversal on the '134 patent, analyzing how self-contradictory expert testimony failed to establish substantial evidence of infringement. It explores the court's strict requirement for clarity when linking expert theory to specific claim limitations, particularly where expert testimony admits to a contradiction regarding sampling input signals versus generated interference.

blogs.title: Prosecution History and the Perils of Narrowing: Was Finesse's 'Three-Signal' Claim a Trap?
blogs.description: This blog examines the '775 patent's analysis regarding whether the plaintiff surrendered claim scope by amending from 'two or three' signals to 'three signals' during prosecution. It offers a doctrinal breakdown of the 'clear and unambiguous disavowal' standard and weighs the risks for patentees who face obviousness rejections but fear narrowing their market coverage too aggressively.

blogs.title: Damages and Procedure: How a JMOL Reversal Erases the $166M Verdict
blogs.description: A procedural analysis focusing on the consequences of a denial of Judgment as a Matter of Law on damages awards. This post discusses the interaction between the Fifth Circuit's JMOL standard (as applied by the Fed. Cir. in cases from the Eastern District of Texas) and the automatic vacatur of lump-sum damages when the underlying infringement theory collapses, regardless of the specific claim construction issues.
